correspondence.component_scope: northeastern_opening_and_upper_lake_chain
correspondence.finding: The selected opening is in a dense lake-and-wetland plain east of the mapped Chukwugwalilik River. Original cartography shows small channels and a south-trending chain of ponds and lakes in the selected upper corridor, but does not establish the complete chosen initial northward passage from the eastern opening into that chain. The nearby river label and shared wetland setting are not substituted for the missing selected connection.

correspondence.component_scope: northwest_turn_and_westward_wetland_transfer
correspondence.finding: The detailed original distinguishes the Chukwugwalilik channel system, small westward tributary linework and intervening lakes. The selected path turns west and then northwest across the wetland plain before taking a westward channel toward the western lake chain. The critical northwest transfer into that western channel is not continuously established by source linework or source prose. This is a substantial through-connection issue, rather than a requirement for exact bends, banks or vertices.

correspondence.component_scope: western_stream_and_lake_chain_to_dall
correspondence.finding: The western approach traverses mapped unnamed stream reaches, small lakes and a larger rounded lake before continuing south toward the northern Dall Lake arm. Stream linework and visible lake outlet/entry necks support this western lake-chain corridor at the ordinary regional scale. These local connections do not resolve the separate upstream transfer into the western channel.

correspondence.component_scope: northern_arm_and_dall_lake_through_passage
correspondence.finding: The selected path reaches the northern connected lake arm and then crosses the broad, continuous Dall Lake waters southwestward through the western lobe. The lake arms, intervening open-water necks, island/peninsula setting and southwestern outlet are visible in the originals. Kinia and Kinak labels occur across connected lake waters in the cartography; they do not erase the distinct Dall Lake identity or make the unselected southern Kinak route part of this selection.

correspondence.component_scope: kinia_outlet_keguk_join_and_lower_river
correspondence.finding: At the southwestern lake outlet the selected corridor continues along the repeatedly labeled Kinia River. Original cartography shows the connected widened reaches and meanders, the separately named Keguk River junction from the north, and the lower route past Chefornak. Generalized selected lines clip individual meanders but remain in this same continuous lower-river corridor. No inter-basin transfer is needed for these lower selected parts.

correspondence.component_scope: actual_coastal_terminal
correspondence.finding: The final selected part remains on the lower Kinia corridor west of Chefornak and ends at the inner coastal mouth, adjacent to the broad open marine water. The original shows the river-mouth opening and its wetland shores. The endpoint is not extended beyond the selected mouth margin, and no current tidal stage, navigability or precise shoreline is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: lake_wetland_and_managed_passage_scope
correspondence.finding: Numerous upper ponds, lakes and wetland channels and the major Dall Lake passage are explicit parts of this review. No selected glacier, dam, reservoir or managed canal is depicted in the inspected sources. The lack of those features does not resolve the unsupported initial and upper wetland connections.

correspondence.component_scope: community_name_context
correspondence.finding: The Village of Chefornak and Naterqak Light Plant presentation pairs Kinia River with Urrsukvaaq and describes river and tributary travel for local hunting and fishing. This is primary community-project usage for the river by Chefornak; it does not establish formal registry status or extend the name across every selected upper lake and wetland channel.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southeastern opening and initial westward mountain-gully approach.
correspondence.finding: The Ocampo relief map shows westward hill drainage entering the plain in the southeastern portion of the selected corridor, south of Sierra El Fuste. The broad opening setting is mapped, but the generalized municipal sheet does not unambiguously select the particular initial gully and its full connection onward. No individual municipal-table arroyo name is assigned to this opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Initial plain entry, northward bends, and northwestward continuation west of Sierra El Fuste and Sierra La Mufa.
correspondence.finding: The original municipal relief map depicts a broad plain, adjoining bajadas and several distinct blue stream approaches. Its mapped streams do not establish the selected continuous through-going connection across this central plain and its changes of direction. Knowing the surrounding sierras and being inside a named subbasin does not supply that missing link.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward plain corridor beside Sierra La Máquina and toward Sierra El Pino, including selected intermediate joins.
correspondence.finding: The original relief map shows north-south blue channel segments and several side approaches in this valley/plain setting. These are positive local channel and terrain observations; the map does not identify the selected chain as one named stream or resolve its full connection back across the central plain. No lake, reservoir or managed-water passage is assumed from an unlabelled join.

correspondence.component_scope: The actual northern endpoint and the immediately preceding links; no substitute nearby endpoint.
correspondence.finding: The municipal relief map places this end of the selection in the plain near Sierra El Pino but does not establish its entry into a named waterbody. CONABIO independently lists El Guaje and Jaco as lakes of the wider priority region, without locating a selected final channel-to-lake connection. The terminal cannot therefore be named Laguna El Guaje on this evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northeastern opening and long southward upper reach, before the lower Negro–Peulla approach.
correspondence.finding: The park plan places the Río Negro headwaters at Cerro Frutilla and describes its northeastern park subcatchment and tributaries. The inspected tourism plate fades into white space and a text panel north of the visible lower corridor; it does not provide usable uninterrupted coverage of the selected opening and entire upper approach. A regional headwater description does not identify each chosen initial link.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower southward approach, Peulla junction and eastern lake entry.
correspondence.finding: The map shows the north-fed approach joining the east-fed Peulla course beside Peulla and entering the eastern end of the lake. The park-plan prose identifies this north-fed river as Negro and describes Peulla joining it near the lake delta. This supports ordinary lower-corridor correspondence, without extending that identification through the unseen upper opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern lake arm, central westward lake passage, inter-fragment join and western lake exit.
correspondence.finding: The inspected map depicts the connected eastern arm through the main Lago Todos Los Santos body to Petrohué at the western outlet. Both selected fragments meet within that same lake passage. The selected route is a lake through-line here, not an independently named river running across the lake.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestward river outlet and upper Petrohué corridor past the falls.
correspondence.finding: The facing tourism-map pages show the lake outlet, Saltos del Petrohué and southwestward upper course. Park-plan prose describes an approximately ten-kilometre southwestward first reach before the river leaves the park at La Nueva Carintia.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastward and southward lower Petrohué valley toward Ralún.
correspondence.finding: The mapped river continues through the lower valley toward Ralún, corresponding to the selected turn and southern continuation. The park plan independently describes the southeastward continuation to the Reloncaví estuary. No present bank alignment or flow-operation claim is made.

correspondence.component_scope: Final lower-river reach and selected sea-class endpoint in the Ralún estuary-head setting.
correspondence.finding: The enlarged tourism map shows the lower river reaching the head of the Reloncaví estuary at Ralún. This agrees with the park-plan account of the river mouth and with the selected coastal endpoint at ordinary regional scale. Exact contemporary delta branches and tidal-bank positions are not asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected eastern headward opening near the Orosí–Cacao area
correspondence.finding: The selected opening runs westward from east of the mapped headwater line before reaching its south-running continuation. Figure 2 instead depicts a headwater arriving from the Orosí side to the northeast. It does not show the selected eastern feeder or its connection. The inspected material does not establish whether this selection represents the same generalized feeder or a distinct upper branch.
correspondence.correspondence: Material pending: selected feeder and through-link not independently established
correspondence.name_scope_limit: The nearby Tempisquito headwater label is not transferred to the unsupported eastern opening. No alternative upper hydronym is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Common upper corridor, Ahogados joining area and middle Tempisque
correspondence.finding: Below the unresolved opening, the selection follows the visible south-running corridor through the Los Ahogados joining area and the Tempisque trunk, past Santa Rita and Hacienda Tempisque into the eastward Guardia–La Guinea/El Viejo corridor. The source maps retain the connected bends and joining network.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary corridor scale downstream of the unresolved headward connection
correspondence.name_scope_limit: Tempisquito and Tempisque are retained as distinct mapped reach usages; an exact transition vertex is not assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower part of first fragment and approach to second fragment
correspondence.finding: The selected eastward and southward turns continue along the mapped Tempisque through the El Viejo/Coache–El Colmenar sector, the Bolsón joining area and the following lower bend. Source linework supports the common trunk rather than an inferred transfer between nearby rivers.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower eastward river, Palo Verde wetland margin and actual stored terminal
correspondence.finding: The final fragment follows the lower Tempisque eastward and then southeast along the Palo Verde lowlands. IMN and OET maps establish the connected river setting; Coleman Figure 1 depicts the broad river and adjacent wetland channels. The actual selected terminal is on this lower inland river passage, upstream of the Tempisque–Bebedero/Gulf continuation. It is not replaced by an ocean-mouth point.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary corridor scale; exact shoreline and local terminal subreach name unasserted

correspondence.component_scope: Successive inland reaches and selected fragment boundary 10715–10716
correspondence.finding: Common connected Tempisque corridor is visible through the downstream joins and across the selected fragment boundary.

correspondence.component_scope: Managed middle-river passages
correspondence.finding: OET describes channel straightening at El Viejo and longitudinal flood-control works in the Guardia–La Guinea setting. Its map and IMN cartography show the continuous selected river corridor. These historical alterations do not imply a missing transfer or require current operating evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake, reservoir and lower wetland passages
correspondence.finding: No lake or reservoir crossing is required along the depicted selection. The lower selection remains on the broad Tempisque river beside the Palo Verde wetlands. Adjacent irrigation channels, wetland pools and crocodile movement paths are not substituted for the selected river.
